pages.text: Two little marks were on the post beside the mill door. Dodo's and Mumu's heights from last spring.
"I want to see how much I've grown!" Mumu stood on tiptoe before the post.
In the morning yard, Dodo pointed to her shadow. "Why measure? Look at your shadow. I know! See? I'm as tall as a tree!"
The morning sun was low, making shadows long. Mumu's reached the wall too.
At midday, Dodo looked down. Her shadow was tiny as a bean!
"I shrank! This morning I was tree-sized!" Dodo hopped and hopped.
Mumu looked at his shadow. Bean-sized too. Shadows seemed to grow and shrink.
Mumu stood with his back flat against the post. "Dad, please measure me!"
Dad made pencil marks. Mumu's was a hand span higher than last spring; Dodo's, half a hand span.
Evening came. Beside her shadow, Dodo stood proud. "See! Evening-me is tree-sized again!" The shadow stretched to the wall.
